orders.objective:
(the operator's session, WS-001 rule 24) the operator opens
Tools, Catalog, chooses Gödel, Escher, Bach and sees ten studied concepts;
they open Levels of description and read its study: the idea in plain words
(the same system is truly described at several levels, each with its own
vocabulary, and no level is the real one) and a situation it serves (a
planning pass, an order, a gate row and a hook refusal are four descriptions
of one afternoon's work), a relations drawing they step through level by
level with the text equivalent naming each level and what it sees of the
next, the ordinary pseudocode of a chunking procedure, an illustrative RxJS
reading where a stream of low-level events becomes a stream of higher-level
ones, public treatments of the idea introduced on their own terms, the
references, the limits (a sealed-off level hides what leaks through) and the
nearby concepts as links (Chunking, Sealed-off levels, Strange loop). They
open Strange loop and step the drawing until it returns to where it began;
they open Isomorphism and Gödel numbering and see one idea become the other's
mechanism, with a small executable encoder they can read the spec of. They
choose Team Topologies, open Collaboration mode, X-as-a-Service mode and
Facilitating mode and read, in one drawing per mode, how two teams exchange
work and where each mode should end; they open Conway's law and read the
homomorphism the drawing shows between a team graph and a system graph, with
the Reverse Conway manoeuvre as its nearby inverse. What the operator learns
is the vocabulary for the levels the platform's mechanisms live on and the
modes its five roles work in; what they decide is which loop or mode to make
visible in the machinery view or a toy next.

## Goal-aligned decisions

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.



Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.


This launchpad is the operator's own DotLn instance. Its purpose is to plan and
run bounded, evidence-gated work orders across the operator's repositories, so
that every change arrives as a pull request the operator reads before it merges,
while the kit itself stays upstream and reaches this fork only through starter
updates. The first workstream is DotLn-Angular, an Nx and Angular monorepo that
serves two outcomes at once: the operator's reference Angular workspace, which a
colleague should recognize as the way the operator builds Angular, and the
operator's sandbox app, one app with sub-apps behind a menu: a scene for
authoring game AI from a toolbox mined from the works the operator reads, a
view of DotLn's machinery where a change to an agent's mechanisms shows what
changes in an example use case, the operator's own digital twin, and side
utilities. Every new idea lives there first as a toy the operator plays with
before promoting the ones that work, for the five UIFA roles, people and
software actors alike. The app is not wired to DotLn core: its data comes from
public mining into its own store, served to the UI through its own API, and it
informs the platform through GitHub issues, never by writing a control record,
so that the app improves the platform, the platform the starter, the starter
this fork, and the fork the app in turn. The critical path runs from registering
that repository in this launchpad, through one witnessed target order that
scaffolds the workspace, to a foundation where a feature is added by convention:
shared libraries, the component taxonomy, events and stores, the sub-app shell,
and a legitimate client-side authentication and permission model. Later
workstreams join the same way: one registration and one planning pass each,
with the fork's own machinery changes cut as self orders beside them.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Unblocks no critical-path gate. It is sandbox catalog side work placed ahead of authentication by the operator's recorded choices (D11; the concept-batch pass). It names a downstream decision, which loop or mode to make visible in the machinery view (WO-016, sequenced after it), but WO-016 does not depend on it. NoOp cost in the records: absence only (no GEB or Team Topologies studies). The cost-table row for WO-024 has metrics null and is stale. No vision passage or role table was supplied, so the order's claim that these two works' vocabulary describes the platform and its five roles' modes cannot be checked against them.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: the same gap as WO-023, new presentation modules with no guard against the shapes WO-034 removes (finding). The analogy rule and the absent-material rule are prose rules enforced by critics, not tools. Tragedy of the commons: 6 to 10 h with a parallel fan-out and two critics per record, and about 180 KB for the executor plus the authors' reads; worker totals sit outside acceptance and tokens are unknown. Drift to low performance: twenty records pass the same checks; no baseline is lowered. Escalation: one more family (relations) and one more rule for WO-038 to size. Success to the successful: it reuses the concept-study-v1 pipeline; appropriate. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: design rounds end only on the operator's word (criterion 8), one of five such orders here (finding). Rule beating: a critic judges per study whether any book passage is quoted, and a close paraphrase of copyrighted text passes that judgment (finding); the minimum of 15 screenshots counts files. Seeking the wrong goal: it advances the sandbox catalog. Its situations use the platform's own vocabulary (planning pass, order, gate row, hook refusal). That keeps the sandbox informative to the platform, but it ties study text to mechanism names that can change (finding).
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost says it removes nothing. It adds about 35 source files, twenty data records, a family, two coverage rows and a rule.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades. The studies are additive behind lazy chunks; a failing record fails studies:check and never ships, and the catalog is otherwise unchanged. The four executable models (Gödel numbering, decision procedure, chunking, Conway's law) fail in their specs, not at runtime.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: WO-040 unblocks no gate on the declared foundation path. The critical-path declaration lists WO-003, WO-004, WO-005, WO-006, WO-007, WO-013 and WO-008. It says every one except WO-008 is closed and that WO-008 does not gate the catalog, scene or machinery examples. WO-040 is second in the sequence and WO-008 is eighth. That order is the operator's recorded schedule: the declaration cites the 2026-10-24 D11 and the concept-batch and quality-pass record, which put study batches at the front as side work, and it says it adds no new priority. So the placement is not a contradiction. The subject lists the vision, the UIFA roles record and the capability table as unavailable and supplies no theses. No vision passage id can be cited, so no vision contradiction can hold. The purpose passage inside the goal standard was read as context only. The blocked outcome the order names is a decision, not a gate: whether to cut the next Movement research batch. The cost line shows a second downstream consumer it does not name. Every flow study reads the `frameOf` function in `flow.ts`, which takes nine positional parameters, and WO-030 in this sequence adds twenty more flow studies. Reshaping it first stops that batch from being written against the nine-parameter builder. NoOp cost in the records: the cost-table row for WO-040 has metrics null, so the NoOp process cost is unknown. In product terms the cost line's gap would remain: 39 loose parameter lists of six or more, two valueN placeholders, 21 flat model keys and three inline projections in the second movement batch; the first batch's boarded residue (eleven time-carrying placeholders, four String(Number(...)) trims, nine names keys); globalThis.matchMedia in the shared drawing; and nineteen flow state labels that read like 'Work queue: Records: 1'. Under NoOp the two movement batches would read as two shapes, which works against the purpose's aim of a reference workspace that a colleague recognizes as the operator's own Angular practice. The `frameOf` debt would also grow with every flow study WO-030 adds. Action beats NoOp because of three records: WO-034, the template reshape, passed first verification with zero operator directions; its machinery share was 0.487; and WO-028, the batch being reshaped, is one of the three of the last eight orders that failed first verification. Reopen the choice if the operator decides that no further Movement or flow batch will be cut, or if WO-030 leaves the sequence.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: guardRefusals is 0 for WO-033 and null for WO-027, WO-034, WO-023 and WO-039, with worsening empty, and the order adds no command. The local goals that could undo one another are inside the order. Criterion 3 keeps the catalog's visual baselines equal to main while criterion 6 rewords nineteen visible sentences and criterion 5 moves the drawing's font sizes to one source (finding, criterion:3). Tragedy of the commons: the executor's context is about 1 MB (about 480 KB for the second batch, about 300 KB for the stream modules, plus WO-034's evidence). That sits on top of an executor cold start of 45,219 bytes (+1,575, no ceiling, verdict unset). Tokens are unknown. Wall-clock is 4 to 6 h plus the fixed cycle. The DOM crawl covers every movement and stream frame at two revisions, plus a label sweep at five sizes and e2e. The stream read is the part that can be separated out (finding, criterion:7). Drift to low performance: the order raises the second batch to the explicit standard the first batch already follows instead of accepting the worse baseline. The cold-start, subject-length and gate-step series show no worsening. Escalation and success to the successful: this is the third standards pass. The non-goals decline a parameter-count lint, and the subject shows no reason why. Each pass re-adapts WO-034's audit, crawl and comparator into its own evidence directory with fresh controls. WO-029 to WO-032 then add eighty studies and no order names a mechanical shape check (finding, criterion:2). Shifting the burden to the intervenor: operatorDirections is 0 for WO-034 (the template) and for WO-039, and 4 for WO-023 (including one CriterionWaived and one RecordCorrected). Corrections are unavailable except for WO-033 (0). Criterion 1 gives the reading to the verifier and leaves the operator only the batch-cut decision. The 24 planning passes since 2026-10-18, two of them on 2026-11-08, are an attention cost across the whole horizon, not one specific to this order. Rule beating: readAmplification is null throughout and stopRefusals is observed only for WO-033 (0), so no rule-beating failure is observed. The order's count and grep checks can still be passed without the intended change: parameter bags, a local motionPoints, window.matchMedia, long functions passed on the executor's own judgment, and 'left' verdicts no check confirms. Criterion 1's random reading of three modules covers this only in part (findings, criterion:2, criterion:4, criterion:5, criterion:7). Seeking the wrong goal: machineryShare runs 0.536, 0.663, 0.487 (WO-034, the nearest analogue), 0.234 and 0.225, with no worsening. The parameter count is the proxy, and criterion 1's reading of the code checks the real goal, so the order stays aimed at readability rather than the count.
orders.removalBalance: Yes, counting named product-code items. By bytes it is unknown. The cost line names these removals: 39 loose parameter lists of six or more, two valueN placeholders, 21 flat model keys and three inline projections. The residue work also removes four String(Number(...)) trims and the globalThis.matchMedia read. It names no new page, family, route, composite, dependency or command. The additions it implies but does not count are: description types (or reuse of existing ones) for the reshaped functions; one breakpoint and font-size declaration that both SCSS and TypeScript read; a glyph regression; nineteen reworded messages; and, on the evidence side, adapted copies of WO-034's four scripts plus before and after audits, a DOM diff, a label sweep and walkthrough frames. No net line or byte figure is given and the cost-table row is null, so the byte balance is unknown rather than failed. One semantic gap: the named removal counts lists of six or more, but criterion 2 sets the limit at more than four parameters. Any function with exactly five parameters is work the cost line does not count (finding, criterion:2).
orders.failureBehavior: Failure falls back to the old behavior at the merge boundary. The order is a refactor that keeps behavior the same plus nineteen reworded messages. It is gated by criterion 3's DOM diff and e2e run and by criterion 8's target gate. If a criterion fails, main keeps today's shapes and text. No later order in the sequence refuses because the reshape did not land: WO-029 and WO-030 can still be written against the old `frameOf`, at the cost of a later reshape. Inside the change, a misnamed nested key or placeholder shows the key or the raw placeholder instead of refusing; fail-closed translation is WO-035's work, later in the sequence. Criterion 3's text-node diff and criterion 4's time-placeholder scan catch that before merge. At runtime, one path has no stated failure mode: the drawing's narrow-screen query, which moves from globalThis.matchMedia to the injected document. With no defaultView or matchMedia (a server render or a test host), it should fall back to the wide sizes rather than throw (finding, criterion:5). The stream verdict step fails safe, because a module marked 'left' is unchanged.

The alternative, translating when a catalog loads and otherwise rendering the data file's English, is not recorded as weighed (finding on failure).
